app.title: Upgrade editor
hint.upgradeBase: Base for all upgrade costs of this building
hint.trackGrowth: Price growth per level when a track has none of its own
chart.label: Cost, total effect and cost-benefit factors per level
changes.none: No changes compared to the game.
error.READONLY: This field is read-only and must match the original
error.ARMOR: Armor values must be finite numbers ≥ 0
error.ARMOR_CONSTANT: The armor constant must be greater than 0
error.ARMOR_REDUCTION: The maximum reduction must be at least 0 and below 1
error.ENEMY_SET: The monster list must not change
error.ENEMY_LOOK: The look must be 1–48 characters (letters, digits, - and _)
error.ENEMY_NUMBER: Monster values must be finite numbers within the allowed range
error.ENEMY_FLAG: Flags must be on or off
error.ENEMY_BUFFS: Buffs must be numbers greater than −1
error.MAX: Max level must be an integer ≥ 1
error.PRICE: Price factor must be greater than 0
plan.costFormula: Cost formula (cost to go from level “level” to “level + 1”)
plan.effectFormula: Benefit formula (effect value at level “level”; level 0 = base value)
plan.functions: Operators: + − * / ^ ( ). Functions: min, max, abs, sqrt, exp, ln, log, log10, floor, ceil, round, pow, sign. Constants: pi, e.
expr.RANGE: Result is not a finite number
expr.MAX: Level count must be between 1 and {limit}
desc.cost: Money it costs to build this building.
desc.upgradeBase: Base price from which all upgrade costs of this building are calculated.
desc.hp: Hit points of the building without upgrades of the health track.
desc.max: Highest upgrade level this track can reach.
desc.step: How much the value grows per level (0.1 = +10% of the base value).
desc.gain: Gain of the first level; later levels grow with the curve growth.
desc.price: Share of the upgrade base paid for the first level.
desc.growth: Factor by which the price rises with every level (1.2 = +20% per level).
desc.gainGrowth: Factor by which the gain grows with every level (1 = constant).
desc.costFormula: Calculates the price for going from level “level” to “level + 1”.
desc.effectFormula: Calculates the effect factor at level “level”; 1 equals the base value.
desc.tracksTable: Default values of the tracks. Buildings without their own curve use them; changes affect every building that uses the track.
desc.track.max: Highest upgrade level of the track.
desc.track.step: Value gain per level (0.1 = +10% of the base value).
desc.track.price: Share of the upgrade base paid for the first level.
desc.track.growth: Factor by which the price rises with every level.
desc.track.energy: Factor by which the energy cost rises with every level.
desc.stat.cost_every: After this many buildings built, the build price rises.
desc.stat.radius: Size of the building in pixels; determines footprint and hit area.
desc.stat.capacity: How much energy the building can store.
desc.stat.links: How many energy beams the building can send at the same time.
desc.stat.build_radius: New buildings can be placed up to this distance (in tiles).
desc.stat.vision: Distance (in tiles) up to which the building clears the fog.
desc.stat.output: Energy the building produces per second.
desc.stat.range: Length of the energy beams in tiles; 1 equals the width of one tile.
desc.stat.rate: Energy per second transferred over one beam.
desc.stat.export: Energy per second converted into money.
desc.stat.attack.damage: Damage per hit (per second for lasers).
desc.stat.attack.range: Attack range in tiles; 1 equals the width of one tile.
desc.stat.attack.chain: Number of targets the lightning jumps to.
desc.stat.attack.min_range: Targets closer than this distance (in tiles) cannot be hit.
desc.stat.attack.splash: Radius of the explosion around the target in tiles.
desc.stat.heal.range: Heal range in tiles; 1 equals the width of one tile.
desc.stat.shield.radius: Radius of the protective field in tiles.
desc.stat.repair.energy: Energy per second the repair consumes.
desc.stat.mobile.speed: Travel speed in pixels per second.
desc.stat.mobile.energy: Energy per second the travel consumes.
chart.scaleNote: Every line is drawn on its own so that its highest value is at the top. You see the course, not the numbers – those are in the tooltip and the table. Move the mouse over a level to see all values, click a name below to hide its line. Shift + click on a name shows only that line, another Shift + click shows all lines again.
values.title: Values of all levels
values.hint: Every upgrade has one row here. You can change any value, and everything that depends on it is recalculated at once. Only “Apply” takes the change over and shows it in the chart. The tools above (parameters, formula) just fill this table for you.
values.noBase: This track has no absolute base value.
values.desc.level: The number of the upgrade. Level 1 is the first upgrade you buy.
values.desc.cost: The money this one upgrade costs.
values.desc.spent: All the money you have spent so far: purchase price of the building plus all upgrades up to and including this level.
values.desc.gain: How much stronger the building gets from exactly this upgrade. 0.4 means 40% of the starting value is added (with 10 health that is 4 more). Above the table you can show the real value instead.
values.desc.effect: How strong the building is after this upgrade compared to the start, as a factor. ×1 is the starting value, ×1.5 means 50% more, ×2 means twice as strong. The same as the total effect, only as a factor (the chart draws only the total effect).
values.desc.single: Is this single upgrade worth it? The value compares what you get (gain in % of the starting value) with what you pay (cost in % of the building price). 100% is a fair price, more is a good deal, less is expensive. At high levels it often drops below 1%, then shown with decimals. If you change it, the price changes.
values.desc.total: Is everything together worth it? Like the value next to it, but for the building with all upgrades up to this level: total effect ÷ money spent, relative to the start (100%). It usually drops because later upgrades get more expensive.
plan.tableModeNote: The values can be edited directly in the values table below.
plan.toolsHint: Parameters and formula calculate all level values, put them into the values table and take them over at once – just like “Apply” in the table. Afterwards you can still adjust single values in the table.
plan.fillHint: Replaces all values of the table and takes them over at once (like “Apply”). Use undo to revert.
error.PARAM: Invalid parameters (price factor and gain > 0, growth > 1)
error.LEVEL_SET: There must be between 1 and 200 levels
error.LEVEL_ID: The level name (id) must be 1–48 characters (letters, digits, - and _)
error.LEVEL_ID_DUPLICATE: This level name is already used by another level
error.LEVEL_CELLS: Map size must be a whole number between 20 and 400 cells
error.LEVEL_MONEY: Starting money must be a whole number of at least 0
error.LEVEL_TIME: Day and night duration must be greater than 0
error.LEVEL_SEED: The seed must be a whole number
error.LEVEL_POSITION: A position must lie between 0 and 1 on both axes
error.LEVEL_TERRAIN: Invalid terrain (counts must be whole numbers ≥ 0, spots need a position between 0 and 1 and a size ≥ 1)
error.CHALLENGE: Invalid challenge (known kind and whole value ≥ 0)
error.ROUTES: Invalid route (two different existing levels, no duplicates)
error.WAVE_ROSTER: Invalid roster entry (known monster, tier ≥ 0, weight > 0; the day roster must not be empty)
levels.d.list: The levels are played in this order. Moving a level also moves its roads on the world map along.
levels.confirmDelete: Really delete level "{id}"? Its roads are removed too.
levels.d.id: Unique name of the level. It is only used internally and for the translations.
levels.d.cellsW: How many fields wide the map is (20 to 400). Bigger maps are slower to generate.
levels.d.cellsH: How many fields high the map is (20 to 400).
levels.d.money: Money you have when the round begins.
levels.d.day: How many seconds the bright part of a day lasts. Solar panels work during this time.
levels.d.night: How many seconds the night lasts. Night waves come with the night roster. Together with the day length this sets how many waves a day has.
levels.d.seed: Number that decides how the random parts of the map look. Same number, same map.
levels.d.dropX: Where you land, from the left edge (0) to the right edge (1).
levels.d.dropY: Where you land, from the top edge (0) to the bottom edge (1).
levels.d.worldAuto: On: the game places the level in a zigzag below the previous one. Off: you set the position yourself (or drag the level on the map above).
levels.d.worldX: Horizontal position on the world map (0 left, 1 right).
levels.d.worldY: Vertical position on the world map (0 top, 1 bottom).
levels.d.structures: Buildings that already stand on the map at the start. Nests and camps send out the waves, turrets defend the enemy.
levels.d.positionX: From the left edge (0) to the right edge (1).
levels.d.positionY: From the top edge (0) to the bottom edge (1).
levels.terrainDesc.plateaus: How many random raised areas are generated. Towers on them shoot farther.
levels.terrainDesc.chasms: How many random chasms cut through the map.
levels.terrainDesc.ponds: How many ponds are placed at random.
levels.terrainDesc.groves: How many small groups of trees are placed.
levels.terrainDesc.forests: How many big forest areas are placed.
levels.terrainDesc.rocks: How many rock groups block the way.
levels.d.spots: Plateaus at a fixed place (not random). Each can have ramps that lead up.
levels.d.spotX: Center from the left edge (0) to the right edge (1).
levels.d.spotY: Center from the top edge (0) to the bottom edge (1).
levels.d.spotSize: Radius of the plateau in fields (at least 1).
levels.d.ramps: A ramp points from the center in a direction (dx, dy), e.g. 1/0 = right, 0/1 = down.
levels.d.challenges: Extra goals shown on the world map when conquering the region (stars).
levels.challengeDesc.core: Conquer with at least this many percent of the core left.
levels.challengeDesc.lost: Conquer losing at most this many buildings.
levels.challengeDesc.days: Conquer the region by this day at the latest.
levels.challengeDesc.combo: Reach a kill combo of at least this size.
levels.challengeDesc.survive: Survive this many days in survival mode.
levels.d.challengeValue: The number the goal asks for (whole number, 0 or more).
levels.d.interval: Seconds between two waves. Smaller means more waves per day.
levels.d.base: How many monsters a wave sends at the start of day 1 (per spawner, before the ground bonus).
levels.d.ramp: How much bigger waves get towards the end of a day. 1.5 means +150% at the very end.
levels.d.nightFactor: Night waves are this many times as big as day waves (1.2 = 20% more).
levels.d.growth: How much bigger waves get with each new day. 0.4 means +40% per day.
levels.waveTimes: {total} waves per day ({day} by day, {night} by night) within {length} seconds; the first comes after 3 seconds.
levels.d.roster: Which monsters appear by day. A higher weight means the monster is picked more often. A monster only appears once the day is reached that is given as tier + 1.
levels.d.night_roster: Which monsters appear by night. Leave it empty to send no special night monsters.
levels.d.monster: Pick a monster; type to search by name.
levels.d.tier: From which day on it appears: day {day}. 0 means from the start.
levels.d.weight: How often it is chosen compared to the other entries (greater than 0).
levels.d.strength: Shows how hard the level gets from day to day. Hover over a column title for an explanation; click a line in the legend to hide it.
levels.d.rounds: How many days the chart and table cover (1 to 60).
levels.strengthDesc.first: Monsters per spawner in the first wave of the day.
levels.strengthDesc.last: Monsters per spawner in the last wave of the day (a night wave).
levels.strengthDesc.units: All monsters one spawner sends during the whole day (at most 30 per wave), plus its share of the extra monsters.
levels.strengthDesc.totalHp: Hit points of all monsters per spawner and day, including the daily HP growth. Averaged over the roster by weight; level and night bonuses of the monsters are not included.
levels.strengthDesc.hpScale: Factor on monster hit points compared to day 1 (grows by 22% per day).
levels.strengthDesc.damageScale: Factor on monster damage compared to day 1 (+8% per day).
levels.strengthDesc.bountyScale: Factor on the money per kill compared to day 1 (+12% per day).
levels.strengthDesc.totalBounty: Money you earn if you defeat everything one spawner sends in a day. Averaged over the roster by weight.
levels.mapLabel: World map with all levels and their roads
levels.d.map: Click a level to edit it, drag it to move it. Pale circles are placed automatically until you move them.
levels.routesAuto: Roads: automatic. Every level is connected to the one before it.
levels.routesCustom: Roads: custom. Levels without any road are connected to the one before them automatically.
values.desc.costFactor: How expensive this upgrade is compared to the purchase price of the building. 1 means just as expensive as the building, 0.5 half as expensive, 2 twice as expensive. If you change it, the price changes. Not drawn in the chart because its line equals the cost.
values.desc.spentFactor: How expensive everything together is compared to the purchase price of the building. 3 means you have spent three times the purchase price up to here. If you change it, the price of this upgrade changes. Not drawn in the chart because its line equals the total cost.
values.desc.totalEffect: By how many percent the building is better than at the start after this upgrade. +100% means twice as strong as at the start, +250% means three and a half times. If you change it, the gain of this level changes, the cost stays.
values.desc.unitCost: How much money 1% of improvement costs you with exactly this upgrade (relative to the value before). Lower is better; if it climbs steeply the upgrade becomes unattractive. If you change it, the price changes, the upgrade itself stays the same.
error.EXTRA_WAVE: Invalid extra appearance (day ≥ 1, day or night, known monster, count 1 to 200)
monsters.sectionDesc.monsters: Browse all monsters and edit their values, buffs and strength per level and time of day.
monsters.sectionDesc.armor: How strongly armor reduces damage – for monsters and buildings.
monsters.sectionDesc.waves: When how many and which monsters come: day and night length, waves, rosters and single extra monsters.
monsters.d.search: Type part of a name to narrow the list.
monsters.d.filterClass: Melee runs up, ranged shoots from afar, air flies over obstacles.
monsters.d.filterFaction: The nest (insects) or the camp (soldiers and machines) sends this monster.
monsters.d.filterFlavor: Normal monsters, bosses, and monsters of the day or the night (night monsters burn at sunrise).
monsters.badgeDesc.class.melee: Walks to its target and attacks up close.
monsters.badgeDesc.class.ranged: Keeps its distance and shoots buildings from afar.
monsters.badgeDesc.class.air: Flies over terrain and walls and needs anti-air.
monsters.badgeDesc.boss: Especially strong monster with a golden ring.
monsters.badgeDesc.nocturnal: Appears at night and burns at sunrise.
monsters.catalogHint: {shown} of {total} monsters. Click a monster to edit it on the right.
monsters.noDesc: This monster has no description yet.
monsters.statsHint: These values apply to the monster on the first level during the day, before time of day, level and the day of the round change anything. Changes apply immediately (undo is possible) and go into the game when you save.
monsters.d.hp: How much damage the monster can take before it dies.
monsters.d.speed: How fast it walks or flies. 56 pixels per second is one tile per second.
monsters.d.damage: How much damage a single attack does.
monsters.d.cooldown: How many seconds the monster waits between two attacks. Smaller means it attacks faster.
monsters.d.reach: From how many tiles away it can attack. 1 is one tile, 0 means right at the target only.
monsters.d.radius: How big the monster is (one tile is 56 pixels). Bigger monsters are easier to hit.
monsters.d.bounty: Money you get for the kill, before the days raise the amount.
monsters.d.armor: Armor reduces incoming damage. How strongly you can see in the Armor section: 0 is no protection.
monsters.d.class: Melee, ranged or air. Decides how the monster moves and attacks.
monsters.d.faction: Nest monsters spawn at nests, camp monsters at camps.
monsters.d.look: Which drawing is used for the monster. Only changes the looks.
monsters.d.boss: Bosses are especially strong and wear a golden ring.
monsters.d.nocturnal: Night monsters burn down at sunrise if they are still alive.
monsters.d.sabotage: Saboteurs head straight for important buildings.
monsters.buffsHint: Buffs make a monster stronger without touching the base value. They are given in percent: 20% means 1.2 times. Night and level are multiplied with each other.
monsters.buff.nightDesc: Applies once to every monster that appears at night.
monsters.buff.levelDesc: Is added for every level: level 1 gets none, level 3 gets double the buff, level 4 triple.
monsters.buff.nightStat: By how many percent {stat} is higher at night. Negative values make it weaker.
monsters.buff.nightArmor: By how many percent armor is higher at night. If the monster has no armor (0), it stays 0.
monsters.buff.levelStat: By how many percent {stat} grows per level (level 2 once, level 3 twice, …).
monsters.buff.levelArmor: By how many percent armor grows per level. If the monster has no armor (0), it stays 0.
monsters.desc.row: Level and time of day of this row. Level 1 gets no level buff, level 2 gets one, level 3 gets two and so on. At night the night buff is added on top.
monsters.desc.hp: Health of the monster after all buffs (without the per-day growth of the rounds).
monsters.desc.damage: Damage of one attack after all buffs.
monsters.desc.speed: Speed in pixels per second after all buffs.
monsters.desc.armor: Armor after all buffs. The higher, the less damage the monster takes.
monsters.desc.reduction: How many percent of every hit are absorbed by armor (armor ÷ (armor + constant), at most the cap from the Armor section).
monsters.desc.effectiveHp: How much damage you really have to deal: health ÷ (1 − reduction). This is the real staying power.
monsters.desc.dps: Damage per second: damage ÷ attack pause. Shows how dangerous the monster is over time.
monsters.desc.bounty: Bounty for the kill. It does not depend on level or time of day, only the day of the round raises it.
monsters.edit.base: Changing this changes the base value ({stat}) – all rows are adjusted.
monsters.edit.level: Changing this changes the level buff for {stat} so that this value is reached on level {level} (base value and night buff stay).
monsters.edit.night: Changing this changes the night buff for {stat} so that this value is reached in this row (base value and level buff stay).
monsters.edit.bounty: Changing this changes the monster's bounty (applies to all rows).
monsters.edit.via.effectiveHp: Calculates the health needed (with the same armor). Then:
monsters.edit.via.dps: Calculates the damage needed (with the same attack pause). Then:
monsters.strengthTitle: Strength over level and time of day
monsters.strengthHint: Rows are the {levels} levels, once for day and once for night. Every cell is editable: a change is first a draft, dependent values are recalculated everywhere, and only “Apply” takes it over. Hovering the chart shows all values, clicking a name hides the line and the column.
monsters.strengthRules: How changes work: level 1 at day changes the base value. Other day rows change the level buff. Night rows change the night buff. Damage reduction changes the armor, effective health the health, damage/s the damage. Hover a cell to see exactly what it changes.
monsters.modeTip: Shows either the real values or how many times (×) larger they are than the base value on level 1 at day.
monsters.noBase: The base value is 0, so a factor is not possible.
monsters.rejected: This value is not possible here (for example health 0, a buff of −100% or lower, or a buff on a base value of 0).
armor.configHint: Armor reduces the damage of every hit. The formula: reduction = armor ÷ (armor + constant), but never more than the cap. Every hit does at least the minimum damage (or less if it was smaller to begin with).
armor.d.constant: At armor of this size exactly half of the damage is absorbed (now: armor {half} = 50%). Larger means armor works more slowly.
armor.d.maxReduction: Armor never absorbs more than this share of the damage, however high it is. 90 means at least 10% always gets through.
armor.d.minDamage: No hit does less than this damage (unless it was smaller to begin with). Continuous beams like the laser count per second. Prevents anything from becoming completely invulnerable.
armor.exampleResult: With armor {armor} and {damage} damage, {share}% is absorbed and {result} damage arrives.
armor.exampleFloor: The minimum damage of {min} applies here.
armor.curveHint: From armor 0 to 300 in steps of ten. All values are in the chart (hover) and in the table. Click a name to hide lines and columns.
armor.desc.reduction: How many percent of the damage armor absorbs.
armor.desc.taken: How many percent of the damage still arrives.
armor.desc.durability: By what factor the target withstands more than its health thanks to armor (for example ×2 means twice the damage is needed).
armor.allTitle: Armor of all buildings and monsters
armor.allHint: Set the base armor of every building and every monster here. In the game, towers raise it further with the Armour upgrade track. Changes apply immediately (undo is possible).
armor.all.name: Name
armor.desc.all.name: Name of the building or monster.
armor.desc.all.type: Whether it is a building or a monster.
armor.desc.all.reduction: How many percent of the damage are absorbed at this armor.
armor.d.entry: Change the base armor. 0 means no protection.
waves.levelHint: Pick a level and set how long day and night last and how the waves are built. The changes are the same as in the Level tab.
waves.d.level: Which level you edit the waves for.
waves.d.day: How many seconds the day lasts. The day monsters come during this time.
waves.d.night: How many seconds the night lasts. At night stronger waves with the night monsters come.
waves.d.dayPick: For which day (round) the wave-by-wave table is shown.
waves.d.rounds: How many days the overview shows (1 to 60).
waves.spawners: This level has {nest} nests and {camp} camps. There are {waves} waves per day; every spawner gets the shown amount in every wave.
waves.extraIntro: On top of the normal rosters you can let single monsters appear on a specific day, for example a boss on day 5 at night.
waves.extraHint: The monsters arrive with the first wave of the chosen section (day or night) of that day and are spread evenly over matching spawners. There has to be at least one wave in that section.
waves.d.extraDay: On which day (round) the monster appears. Day 1 is the first round.
waves.d.extraPhase: Whether it appears with the first day wave or the first night wave.
waves.d.extraCount: How many of them appear in total (1 to {max}).
waves.daysHint: Calculated from the game formulas: per day you see how many monsters of each kind appear per spawner on average. The pick of monsters is random by weight, so these are averages. Extra monsters (★) come on top.
waves.desc.day: The number of the day (round). A click selects it for the wave-by-wave table.
waves.desc.monsters: Which monsters come on average per spawner on this day.
waves.desc.no: The number of the wave on this day.
waves.desc.time: Second of the round in which the wave starts.
waves.desc.phase: Whether the wave comes by day or at night.
waves.desc.units: How many monsters every spawner gets in this wave.
waves.desc.extras: Extra monsters you entered for this wave.
waves.fallbackNote: * No monster of the roster fits this spawner or this tier, so the default monster of the faction comes.
overview.open: Open the building and expand this track
groups.title: Areas
groups.hint: Sort upgrades into your own areas (e.g. “Offense”, “Economy”) with as many subheadings as you like. One upgrade may sit in any number of areas and subheadings at once. This only organizes the editor – the game never sees it.
groups.none: No areas yet. Create the first one with “+ Area”.
groups.pick: Pick an area from the list to edit it.
groups.name: Area name
groups.d.name: Free text, at most 60 characters. Two areas (or two subheadings in the same area) must not share a name.
groups.d.filter: Shows only the upgrades of this area in the table, split by its subheadings. “All upgrades” shows everything.
groups.areaEmpty: This area is still empty. Add upgrades on the left.
groups.confirmDelete: Delete the area “{name}”? The upgrades themselves stay unchanged.
groups.confirmDeleteSection: Delete the subheading “{name}”? The upgrades themselves stay unchanged.
error.GROUPS: Invalid areas (wrong structure or too many entries)
error.GROUP_NAME: The name of an area or subheading is missing or longer than 60 characters
error.GROUP_DUPLICATE: A name or an upgrade appears twice
error.GROUP_ITEM: Unknown upgrade in an area (the building or track does not exist)
balance.hint: Read-only check of the current values. Every warning is a hint, not an error. A click jumps to the matching place. The thresholds only apply to this view and are not saved.
balance.d.killSeconds: The longest the strongest tower (base stats, without upgrades and research) may need for a normal monster.
balance.d.bossFirstDay: Bosses that can appear earlier (roster or extra monsters) are reported.
balance.rule.upgrades: Tracks with at least one level that is clearly worse than comparable levels of other buildings (below {minLevelShare} % of the typical “Level factor” of the same level). Late levels getting weaker in general is intended and not reported.
balance.rule.monsters: Time the strongest tower with base stats needs for a monster (armor included, no critical hits), in the worst level and time of day in which it appears. Limit: {killSeconds} s, bosses {bossKillSeconds} s.
balance.rule.starters: Every roster (day and night) needs at least one monster of tier 0, otherwise only the faction's fallback monster comes on the first day.
balance.rule.bosses: Bosses should not come before day {bossFirstDay} (tier in the roster = day − 1).
balance.upgradeText: {building} · {track}: noticeably weak from level {first} ({count} of {levels} levels), weakest level {at} with {worst} instead of the usual {typical}
balance.monsterText: {monster}: {seconds} s instead of at most {limit} s (level {level}, {phase}, effective life {hp}; best tower {tower} with {dps} damage/s)
balance.monsterTextUnused: {monster}: {seconds} s instead of at most {limit} s (appears in no level, computed for level {level}, {phase}; effective life {hp}; best tower {tower} with {dps} damage/s)
balance.starterText: Level {level} ({id}), {phase}: no monster of tier 0 – the earliest only comes from tier {lowest}
balance.bossRoster: Level {level} ({id}): boss {monster} can already come on day {day} ({phase} roster)
balance.bossExtra: Level {level} ({id}): boss {monster} comes as an extra monster on day {day} ({phase})
balance.f.minLevelShare: Minimum share of the typical value (%)
balance.d.minLevelShare: A level counts as weak if it gives less than this share of what upgrades of the same level usually give across all buildings (median “Level factor”). 25 means less than a quarter of the usual value.
